sub_questions.question: Do I need to delete and re-upload the whole document after fixing a typo, or will it just update?

claims.claim: Edits to an existing document aren't re-indexed, so the old text will keep showing up in retrieval.
claims.guide_evidence: When a document is edited and saved, it is re-processed through these same four stages before its chunks are available for retrieval again

claims.claim: The customer should delete the document and upload the corrected file as a new one.
claims.guide_evidence: When a document is edited and saved, it is re-processed through these same four stages before its chunks are available for retrieval again; a newly indexed document is not searchable mid-processing.

customer_safety_issues: Gives incorrect instruction that would lead the customer to needlessly delete and re-upload documents, based on a false claim about how edits work.
evaluation.rationale: The guide says an edited and saved document is automatically re-processed through Parse, Enrich, Chunk and Embed/Index. The answer says edits aren't re-indexed and tells the customer to delete and re-upload, which contradicts the guide. The error is confident and leads to unnecessary work, and could count against document or storage quotas. It is not a billing or security matter, so I rated it major rather than critical.
